title: Meridian Cloud faces EU inquiry over data egress fees
author: Hannah Price
text:
The European Commission has opened a formal inquiry into Meridian Cloud's data egress fees, examining whether charges that can reach 9% of a typical customer's monthly bill discourage businesses from moving data to rival providers.

The Commission said it would assess whether the fees, charged when customers transfer data out of Meridian's network, amount to an unfair barrier to switching under the bloc's digital competition rules. The inquiry follows complaints from two trade groups representing European software companies.

Meridian Cloud said it would cooperate fully. "We believe our fees are transparent and competitive, and we already waive transfer charges for customers who leave our platform," a company spokesperson said.

Egress fees have drawn growing scrutiny on both sides of the Atlantic. Critics argue they lock customers in, since moving large data sets can cost more than storing them for years. Providers counter that the fees reflect real network costs.

The Commission did not set a deadline. Formal inquiries of this kind typically run for 12 to 18 months and can end with binding commitments or fines of up to 10% of global turnover. The investigation lands a week after Meridian agreed to buy Vireo Analytics.
